Epson LifeStudio Pop And Flex Land In Australia

Epson is bringing its LifeStudio Pop and Flex smart mini projectors to Australia, combining 4K PRO-UHD projection, automated setup, Google TV and Sound by Bose in compact lifestyle-focused designs.

Jason Sexton 15th September, 2026 · 3 min read
1 reading now
Share

Sponsored by
0:00 / 2:38
Instaread

Epson has confirmed the Australian arrival of its LifeStudio smart projector range, with the LifeStudio Pop EF-62B and LifeStudio Flex EF-73 set to reach local retailers this month. The announcement marks the latest stage in a rollout first detailed by StereoNET last year, when Epson introduced its broader LifeStudio family and collaboration with Bose. That original launch established a range spanning portable lifestyle projectors through to an ultra-short-throw model, all combining Epson's 3LCD projection technology with Google TV and Sound by Bose.

Epson expanded on that strategy earlier this year with deeper integration of the LifeStudio platform, including plans to introduce Google TV with Gemini across selected models.

Now, two of the portable models are officially heading to Australian homes. The more compact LifeStudio Pop EF-62B uses Epson's latest Triple Core Engine and 3LCD projection system, delivering 4K PRO-UHD images at up to 150 inches. Brightness is rated at 700 lumens for both white and colour output.

Automatic focus, keystone correction, screen fit, obstacle avoidance and wall-colour adjustment are designed to reduce setup time. At the same time, the built-in Google TV provides direct access to streaming services without an external media player. Audio is handled by an integrated Sound by Bose system, continuing the collaboration that became one of the defining features of the original LifeStudio launch.

The LifeStudio Flex EF-73 moves further up the range with 1,000 lumens of white and colour brightness, while retaining 4K PRO-UHD projection, Google TV, Sound by Bose and the same suite of automatic image-adjustment features.

Where the Flex differs most is in its physical design. A built-in gimbal allows the projector to be angled more freely around a room, while integrated ambient lighting is intended to make the unit part of the surrounding space rather than something that disappears when the movie finishes.

Epson has also fitted a wireless charging pad to the EF-73, reinforcing the company's positioning of LifeStudio as a broader lifestyle product rather than a conventional portable projector. Both models use Epson's three-chip 3LCD architecture, which produces equal white and colour brightness and avoids the colour-wheel arrangement used by many compact single-chip DLP projectors.

The Australian launch also continues a broader shift in Epson's projector strategy towards products designed for less permanent installations. Rather than requiring a dedicated theatre space, LifeStudio is aimed at users who want a large projected image but still expect the portability, streaming integration and automated setup associated with contemporary consumer electronics.

The Epson LifeStudio Pop EF-62B is priced at A$1,499 and LifeStudio Flex EF-73 at A$2,199 will be available through authorised Epson retailers.

For more information, visit Epson
